chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh al-Nakhaʿi, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from ʿAli ibn Yaqtin, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a well into which a pigeon, a chicken, a mouse, a dog, or a cat falls. He said: It suffices you to draw from it buckets, for that purifies it, if Allah, Exalted is He, wills.

The sound approach concerning these reports is one of two possibilities: either that he عليه السلام answered regarding the ruling of some of what the question included, namely the mouse and the bird, and relied regarding the ruling of the rest upon what is well known from his doctrine or from other reports that became widespread from them عليهم السلام; or secondly, that there is no contradiction in that, because his statement, 'draw from it buckets,' is a plural indicating abundance, which means what exceeds ten, and it is not impossible that what is intended by it is forty buckets, in accordance with what the earlier reports contain. If what was intended were less than ten, its plural would come on the pattern afʿilah rather than fiʿāl. Moreover, knowledge has been established that impurity has occurred, and by drawing forty buckets the ruling of impurity is also removed, and that is known; whereas anything less than that belongs to the category of solitary reports, so practice should be according to what we have stated.

key_terms.أَخْبَارِ الْآحَادِ: solitary reports that do not convey the highest level of certainty
key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ دَلْوًا: forty buckets, understood here as the operative quantity
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose ruling is being discussed
key_terms.تَنْزَحَ: to draw out water from a well

ai.seo_question: How is the hadith about drawing buckets from a contaminated well understood in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report addresses the fiqh ruling on a well into which certain animals have fallen, stating that drawing buckets of water purifies it. The accompanying discussion reconciles this wording with other reports by arguing either that only some cases were directly intended or that the plural 'buckets' can denote a larger number, specifically forty, thereby supporting the established ruling concerning removal of najasah.
